overall_summary: Space-themed content focusing on extreme planetary conditions and mind-bending cosmic anomalies consistently outperforms all other categories. Meanwhile, cognitive psychology and brain-related facts struggle to gain initial traction, even with repeated uploads.

winning_patterns.pattern: Extreme Cosmic Anomalies & Bizarre Planetary Weather
winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet of Burning Ice' (1,055 views), 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' (984 views), and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (634 views) are the channel's top performers.
winning_patterns.action: Focus heavily on extreme space science, highlighting bizarre planetary environments, cosmic scale, and mind-bending physics with highly visual titles.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (max 53 views across multiple attempts) and 'Your Brain Is Hiding This From You' (38 views) consistently fail to capture viewer interest.
weak_patterns.action: Pause production on standard brain facts and memory tricks, redirecting resources to high-performing space and cosmic mystery niches.

next_video.concept: The Planet That Is Being Eaten Alive! 🪐
next_video.opening_direction: Start with a hyper-realistic CGI animation of a planet being stretched into an egg shape by its host star's gravity.
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that this cosmic giant is literally being consumed piece by piece and has less than 10 million years left to live.
next_video.reason: Leverages the proven high-performance pattern of extreme planetary anomalies while introducing a dramatic, time-sensitive cosmic event to drive high retention.

experiment: Test a 'What-If' space scenario (e.g., 'What If the Moon Was Made of Glass?') to see if the high engagement of space facts translates to speculative cosmic storytelling.
